literal: Heart being pleased than giving, it is better indeed, face being pleased sweet-worded-one to be if obtained.
translation: It is even better than giving with a joyful heart, if one can speak sweet words with a cheerful face.
modern: உள்ளம் மகிழ்ந்து ஒரு பொருளைக் கொடுப்பதை விட, முகம் மலர்ந்து இனிய சொற்களைக் கூறுபவனாக இருக்க முடிந்தால் அது மிகவும் நல்லது.
explanation: This couplet compares two virtuous acts: giving generously and speaking sweetly. The phrase 'அகன் அமர்ந்து ஈதல்' refers to giving a gift with a willing, joyful heart. However, the poet states that 'முகன் அமர்ந்து இன்சொலன் ஆகப் பெறின்'—having a cheerful face and speaking pleasant words—is even better. The comparative suffix 'இன்' in 'ஈதலின்' combined with 'நன்றே' (it is better indeed) establishes that sweet speech with a smiling face surpasses even heartfelt charity. This emphasizes that kind words are a supreme virtue, accessible to everyone and deeply impactful.
